---
title: "Global maps of genotype assignment completeness by region"
author: "Angela"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: html_document
---

## Objectives
* Map % of samples assigned a genotype by each method (GenoFlu, Genin2) across global regions
* Region polygons are country polygons dissolved to UN subregions, filled by % assigned
* One map file per method (since 2020, matching the assignment-rate panel in compare_genotyping)

Modern GIS stack: `sf` + `rnaturalearth` (country polygons) + `countrycode` (name->ISO3 join).
`maptools`/`rgeos`/`rgdal` are retired (removed from CRAN) and are not used.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(gtools)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(countrycode)
library(ggrepel)     # repel overlapping region labels
library(scatterpie)  # per-region genotype pies on the map
library(RColorBrewer)

sf_use_s2(FALSE)  # planar ops for dissolve/centroid; avoids s2 edge errors on subregion unions

# Robinson projection (standard for world maps)
crs_robin <- "+proj=robin +lon_0=0 +datum=WGS84 +units=m +no_defs"

plot.theme <- theme(
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  panel.background = element_rect("grey95"),
  axis.line        = element_line(colour = "black"),
  text             = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
  legend.text      = element_text(size = 8),
  axis.text.x      = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1)
)
```

```{r paths}
# per-sample combined output from compare_genotyping (has region, collection_date, assigned flags)
# NB: use sort(), not gtools::mixedsort(), to pick the newest dated folder.
# mixedsort() reads the dashes in "2026-06-25" as minus signs (month -> -06), which
# reverses the date order so tail(1) would grab the OLDEST file. ISO dates sort
# chronologically under plain sort().
f.combined <- list.files(".", pattern = "combined_genotyping_meta\\.csv",
                         recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE) %>% sort() %>% tail(1)
cat("combined input:", f.combined, "\n")

# country -> region lookups (union of NCBI + GISAID for max country coverage)
f.lookup <- c("../../01a_ncbi/clean_ncbi/lookups/country_continent.csv",
              "../../01b_gisaid/clean_gisaid/lookups/country_continent.csv")

f.out <- paste0(Sys.Date(), "_map/")
if (!dir.exists(f.out)) dir.create(f.out)

# small export size (kept at 300 dpi) for later cowplot/magick compositing
map_w <- 7
map_h <- 4.1
```

```{r region-setup}
region_ord <- c(
  "Western Europe", "Northern Europe", "Southern Europe", "Eastern Europe",
  "Western Africa", "Northern Africa", "Southern Africa", "Eastern Africa", "Middle Africa",
  "Western Asia", "Central Asia", "Southern Asia", "South-Eastern Asia", "Eastern Asia",
  "North America", "Central America", "Caribbean", "South America",
  "Oceania", "Antarctica"
)
```

## Read data and compute % assigned by region (since 2020)

```{r read-assign, message=FALSE}
# all samples with a valid region. Filter on collection_year, not collection_date:
# every sample has at least a year, but collection_date is blank when the original date
# is incomplete (year-only "2020" or year-month "2020-04"), so date-based filters silently
# drop those partial-date records (incl. many 2020+ samples).
samp <- read_csv(f.combined, col_types = cols(.default = "c")) %>%
  mutate(collection_year  = as.integer(collection_year),
         assigned_genin   = assigned_genin   == "TRUE",
         assigned_genoflu = assigned_genoflu == "TRUE") %>%
  filter(region %in% region_ord)

# % assigned by region, 2020-2025 only (drives the pct maps)
reg_assign <- samp %>%
  filter(collection_year >= 2020) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(
    n           = n(),
    pct_genin   = mean(assigned_genin)   * 100,
    pct_genoflu = mean(assigned_genoflu) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

reg_assign
```

## Build region polygons (countries dissolved to UN subregions)

```{r build-regions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# country -> region from the project lookups; route names through ISO3 for a robust join
lookup <- f.lookup %>%
  map_dfr(~read_csv(.x, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))) %>%
  transmute(country, region,
            iso3 = countrycode(country, "country.name", "iso3c", warn = FALSE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(iso3)) %>%
  distinct(iso3, .keep_all = TRUE)
# NB: NCBI ("USA") and GISAID ("United States") both normalise to ISO3 "USA", so distinct()
# safely collapses them to one polygon (verified: no ISO3 maps to >1 region across the lookups).
# 5 entries fail to resolve to an ISO3 and so get NO coloured polygon (drawn as grey basemap):
# Kosovo (countrycode lacks a default iso3c match) + Torgersen/Roberts/Livingston/Gough Island
# (sub-Antarctic islets absent from Natural Earth's country layer). Their samples still count
# toward their region's stats, which aggregate on the pre-assigned `region` column, not ISO3.

# Natural Earth country polygons; iso_a3_eh fixes the -99 codes (France, Norway, ...)
world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>%
  mutate(iso3 = if_else(is.na(iso_a3_eh) | iso_a3_eh == "-99", adm0_a3, iso_a3_eh)) %>%
  left_join(lookup %>% select(iso3, region), by = "iso3")

# dissolve countries into one multipolygon per region, then project to Robinson
region_poly <- world %>%
  filter(!is.na(region)) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(.groups = "drop") %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  st_transform(crs_robin)

# polygons joined to the 2020-2025 assignment summary (for the pct + 2020-2025 N maps)
region_sf <- region_poly %>% left_join(reg_assign, by = "region")

# faint basemap = all land (incl. regions with no assignment data)
basemap <- world %>% st_make_valid() %>% st_transform(crs_robin)

# graticule: faint lat/long lines every 20 deg (built in lon/lat, projected to Robinson)
graticule <- st_graticule(x = c(-180, -90, 180, 90), crs = st_crs(4326),
                          lon = seq(-180, 180, 20),
                          lat = seq(-80, 80, 20)) %>%
  st_transform(crs_robin)

# label point per region: a representative interior point (centred, guaranteed on land)
region_labels <- region_sf %>%
  filter(region %in% region_ord) %>%
  st_point_on_surface() %>%
  select(region)

# manual label nudges (fractions of map width/height); their st_point_on_surface
# interior points sit slightly off where the label reads best
map_w_span <- diff(st_bbox(region_labels)[c("xmin", "xmax")])
map_h_span <- diff(st_bbox(region_labels)[c("ymin", "ymax")])
nudge_label <- function(region_name, dx_frac = 0, dy_frac = 0) {
  i <- region_labels$region == region_name
  region_labels$geometry[i] <<- region_labels$geometry[i] +
    c(dx_frac * map_w_span, dy_frac * map_h_span)
}
# Antarctica: left so it clears the meridian, and down onto the continent
nudge_label("Antarctica", dx_frac = -0.25, dy_frac = -0.04)
# Caribbean: down a touch off the island cluster
nudge_label("Caribbean", dy_frac = -0.03)
region_labels <- st_set_crs(region_labels, crs_robin)

# additional manual nudges specified in DEGREES (dx = lon, dy = lat): project the label to
# lon/lat, add the degree offset, and project back to Robinson. Exact per-point, so a
# "10 deg" shift means the same in geographic terms regardless of projection distortion.
nudge_label_deg <- function(region_name, dx_deg = 0, dy_deg = 0) {
  i     <- which(region_labels$region == region_name)
  pt_ll <- st_transform(region_labels$geometry[i], 4326)
  moved <- st_sfc(st_point(as.numeric(st_coordinates(pt_ll)) + c(dx_deg, dy_deg)), crs = 4326)
  region_labels$geometry[i] <<- st_transform(moved, crs_robin)
}
nudge_label_deg("North America",   dx_deg = -4, dy_deg = 5)  # up 5, left 4
nudge_label_deg("South America",   dx_deg = -6, dy_deg = 10) # up 10, left 6
nudge_label_deg("Eastern Africa",  dx_deg = 10, dy_deg = 8)  # up 8, right 10
nudge_label_deg("Western Asia",    dy_deg = 5)              # up 5
nudge_label_deg("Southern Asia",   dx_deg = -3, dy_deg = 3)  # up 3, left 3
nudge_label_deg("Northern Europe", dx_deg = -10, dy_deg = -2) # left 10, down 2
nudge_label_deg("Eastern Europe",  dx_deg = 10, dy_deg = 3)  # up 3, right 10
nudge_label_deg("Northern Africa", dx_deg = -5, dy_deg = 5)  # up 5, left 5
nudge_label_deg("Antarctica",      dx_deg = 5)              # right 5
region_labels <- st_set_crs(region_labels, crs_robin)

# two-line variant of each label (break at the first space, e.g. "South-Eastern\nAsia") so
# boxed labels centre over their region and neighbours (W/N Africa, W/S Asia, S/W Europe) separate
region_labels <- region_labels %>% mutate(region_lab = sub(" ", "\n", region))

# extra degree nudges for the boxed (two-line, repelled) labels only -- the plain-label maps
# keep the positions above. Same lon/lat round-trip as nudge_label_deg(), but returns a copy.
shift_label_deg <- function(lab, region_name, dx_deg = 0, dy_deg = 0) {
  i     <- which(lab$region == region_name)
  pt_ll <- st_transform(lab$geometry[i], 4326)
  moved <- st_sfc(st_point(as.numeric(st_coordinates(pt_ll)) + c(dx_deg, dy_deg)), crs = 4326)
  lab$geometry[i] <- st_transform(moved, crs_robin)
  lab
}
region_labels_boxed <- region_labels %>%
  shift_label_deg("North America",   dx_deg = -6, dy_deg = -5) %>%  # left 6, down 5
  shift_label_deg("Central America", dy_deg = -2) %>%               # down 2
  shift_label_deg("Eastern Europe",  dx_deg = -6, dy_deg = -4) %>%  # left 6, down 4
  shift_label_deg("Eastern Asia",    dx_deg = -5) %>%               # left 5
  shift_label_deg("Northern Africa", dy_deg = 2) %>%                # up 2
  shift_label_deg("Western Asia",    dy_deg = -4) %>%               # down 4
  shift_label_deg("Western Europe",  dx_deg = -3) %>%               # left 3
  shift_label_deg("Northern Europe", dx_deg = -3) %>%               # left 3
  shift_label_deg("Antarctica",      dx_deg = 15)                   # right 15
```

## Region -> country lookup table

```{r region-country-lookup, message=FALSE}
# concatenated country list per region, for reference (built from the raw source lookups)
region_country_lookup <- f.lookup %>%
  map_dfr(~read_csv(.x, col_types = cols(.default = "c"))) %>%
  distinct(country, region) %>%
  filter(!is.na(country), !is.na(region)) %>%
  mutate(region = factor(region,
                         levels = c(region_ord,
                                    setdiff(sort(unique(region)), region_ord)))) %>%
  arrange(region, country) %>%
  group_by(region) %>%
  summarise(n_countries = n(),
            countries   = paste(country, collapse = ", "),
            .groups = "drop")

region_country_lookup
write.csv(region_country_lookup, paste0(f.out, "region_country_lookup.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Map base + outputs

```{r map-base}
# shared base: grey basemap + region polygons (fill set per map) + centred labels.
# `data` defaults to the 2020-2025 region_sf but can be swapped (e.g. N maps by date range).
# `labels = FALSE` drops the region text (for clean, label-free versions of a map).
# `alpha` sets the region-fill transparency (lower = more transparent for label contrast).
# `label_style = "boxed"` draws larger, bold, two-line repelled labels on a faint, borderless white
# backing box (fill = alpha("white", 0.45)); "plain" = original text.
base_map <- function(fill_col, data = region_sf, labels = TRUE, alpha = 0.6,
                     label_style = "plain") {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = graticule, color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = basemap,   fill = "grey95", color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_sf(data = data, aes(fill = .data[[fill_col]]),
            color = "white", linewidth = 0.3, alpha = alpha) +
    {if (labels && label_style == "plain")
      geom_sf_text(data = region_labels, aes(label = region), size = 3.2)} +
    {if (labels && label_style == "boxed")
      # repel (fixed seed) so the crowded Europe / N Africa-W Asia / Middle-E Africa boxes separate
      geom_label_repel(data = region_labels_boxed, aes(label = region_lab, geometry = geometry),
                       stat = "sf_coordinates", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold",
                       lineheight = 0.8, fill = alpha("white", 0.45), linewidth = 0,
                       label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"), box.padding = unit(0.05, "lines"),
                       point.size = NA, min.segment.length = Inf, max.overlaps = Inf,
                       seed = 42)} +
    # NB: no scale bar or north arrow -- both are cartographically meaningless on a
    # whole-world Robinson projection (and ggspatial::annotation_scale() errors because the
    # panel corner inverse-projects to NaN outside the projection lens).
    coord_sf(datum = NA, expand = FALSE) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(text            = element_text(size = 13),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"),
          legend.title     = element_text(hjust = 0.5, vjust = 0.5))
}
```

### N samples (by date range)

```{r map-n, fig.width=6, fig.height=3.5}
# region polygons joined to a per-region sample count over a year window.
# ymin/ymax NULL = unbounded; with both NULL, every sample is counted.
region_n_sf <- function(ymin = NULL, ymax = NULL) {
  d <- samp
  if (!is.null(ymin)) d <- filter(d, collection_year >= ymin)
  if (!is.null(ymax)) d <- filter(d, collection_year <= ymax)
  region_poly %>% left_join(count(d, region, name = "n"), by = "region")
}

# legend_pos = "bottom" (default, wide horizontal colourbar), "right" (vertical colourbar) or
# "top" (horizontal colourbar above the map, title directly above the bar, left-justified).
# Right-legend layout uses wider/shorter export dims since the key sits beside the map, not below.
# range_lab = NULL gives a plain "N H5Nx samples" legend title (used for the all-dates maps).
map_n <- function(ymin, ymax, range_lab, file_suffix,
                  legend_pos = "bottom", w = map_w, h = map_h, alpha = 0.6,
                  label_style = "plain") {
  # top legend: title on one line above the bar ("N H5Nx samples, 1996-2025"; saves height);
  # others keep the two-line title
  leg_title <- if (is.null(range_lab)) "N H5Nx samples" else
    paste0("N H5Nx samples", if (legend_pos == "top") ", " else "\n", range_lab)
  p <- base_map("n", data = region_n_sf(ymin, ymax), alpha = alpha, label_style = label_style) +
    scale_fill_distiller(palette = "YlGnBu", direction = 1, trans = "log10",
                         name = leg_title, na.value = "grey90",
                         breaks = c(10, 100, 1000, 10000))
  if (legend_pos == "top") {
    # legend above the map (panel E in 07_summarize*): minimises gaps in the composite
    p <- p + guides(fill = guide_colourbar(direction = "horizontal")) +
      theme(legend.position       = "top",
            legend.justification  = "left",
            legend.title.position = "top",
            legend.title          = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold", size = 13.75,
                                                 margin = margin(0, 0, 1, 0)),
            legend.text           = element_text(size = 9),
            legend.key.width      = unit(1.1, "cm"),  # colourbar length = 5x key width (~5.5 cm)
            legend.key.height     = unit(0.35, "cm"),
            legend.margin         = margin(0, 0, 0, 60),  # nudge legend right of the map edge
            legend.box.spacing    = unit(2, "pt"))
  }
  if (legend_pos == "right") {
    p <- p + guides(fill = guide_colourbar(direction = "vertical")) +
      theme(legend.position  = "right",
            legend.key.width  = unit(0.5, "cm"),
            legend.key.height = unit(1.4, "cm"),
            legend.title      = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold"),
            plot.margin       = margin(r = 10))  # room for the bold legend title
  }
  ggsave(paste0(f.out, "map_n_samples_", file_suffix, ".pdf"), p, width = w, height = h)
  ggsave(paste0(f.out, "map_n_samples_", file_suffix, ".png"), p, width = w, height = h)
  p
}

p_map_n_2020 <- map_n(2020, NULL, "2020-2025",   "2020-2025")
p_map_n_1996 <- map_n(1996, NULL, "1996-2025",   "1996-2025")
p_map_n_all  <- map_n(NULL, NULL, NULL, "all-dates")

# legend-on-the-right versions (own, wider/shorter export dims; less transparent fill -- these
# are reused in another script, where the stronger colours read better). Boxed labels so the
# region names stay legible at composite size (panel E in 07_summarize*).
p_map_n_1996_right <- map_n(1996, NULL, "1996-2025", "1996-2025_legend-right",
                            legend_pos = "right", w = 7.6, h = 3.6, alpha = 0.7,
                            label_style = "boxed")
p_map_n_all_right  <- map_n(NULL, NULL, NULL, "all-dates_legend-right",
                            legend_pos = "right", w = 7.6, h = 3.6, alpha = 0.7,
                            label_style = "boxed")
p_map_n_2020

# legend-on-top versions for the 07_summarize* composites (panel E): horizontal colourbar above
# the map, title directly above it (left-justified), boxed labels as in the right versions.
# Near-opaque fill (alpha 0.95): the faint label backing boxes keep the region names readable
p_map_n_1996_top <- map_n(1996, NULL, "1996-2025", "1996-2025_legend-top",
                          legend_pos = "top", w = 7.6, h = 4.3, alpha = 0.95,
                          label_style = "boxed")
p_map_n_all_top  <- map_n(NULL, NULL, NULL, "all-dates_legend-top",
                          legend_pos = "top", w = 7.6, h = 4.3, alpha = 0.95,
                          label_style = "boxed")
p_map_n_1996
p_map_n_all
p_map_n_1996_right
p_map_n_all_right
p_map_n_1996_top
p_map_n_all_top
```

### Genotype pies by region (2020-2025)

```{r map-pies, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=4.1}
# One pie per global region, centred on the region centroid (pushed down so the bumped-up
# label clears it). Pie area is proportional to the number of samples ASSIGNED a genotype
# by that method (sqrt scaling), with a small floor so sparse regions stay visible.
# Slices are the top genotypes globally (2020-2025); rarer ones collapse into "Other".

# map extent (full region polygons) drives pie sizing and legend placement
bb_pie     <- st_bbox(region_poly)
pie_w_span <- bb_pie["xmax"] - bb_pie["xmin"]
pie_h_span <- bb_pie["ymax"] - bb_pie["ymin"]

# region centroids in Robinson space (geographic centre; may sit offshore, fine as a marker)
region_cent <- region_poly %>%
  st_centroid() %>%
  mutate(x = st_coordinates(.)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(region, x, y)

r_max   <- 0.052 * pie_w_span   # radius of the largest pie
r_floor <- 0.013 * pie_w_span   # minimum radius so small regions remain legible

# wide genotype-count table per region for one method, lumped to top `n_top` + "Other"
pie_data <- function(method, n_top = 9) {
  gcol <- paste0(method, "_geno")
  acol <- paste0("assigned_", method)
  a <- samp %>%
    filter(collection_year >= 2020, .data[[acol]]) %>%
    transmute(region, geno = .data[[gcol]])
  ord  <- a %>% count(geno, sort = TRUE) %>% slice_head(n = n_top) %>% pull(geno)
  cols <- c(ord, "Other")
  wide <- a %>%
    mutate(geno = if_else(geno %in% ord, geno, "Other")) %>%
    count(region, geno) %>%
    group_by(region) %>% mutate(n_assigned = sum(n)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = geno, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
    left_join(region_cent, by = "region") %>%
    filter(!is.na(x))
  for (cc in setdiff(cols, names(wide))) wide[[cc]] <- 0   # ensure every slice column exists
  wide$r <- pmax(r_floor, r_max * sqrt(wide$n_assigned / max(wide$n_assigned)))
  list(df = as.data.frame(wide), cols = cols, max_n = max(wide$n_assigned))
}

# qualitative palette: distinct non-grey hues for the named genotypes, grey reserved for "Other".
# (Set1's 9th colour is grey, which would clash with "Other", so use an explicit list instead.)
geno_cols_base <- c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8", "#4DAF4A", "#984EA3", "#FF7F00",
                    "#FFD92F", "#A65628", "#F781BF", "#1B9E77", "#66A61E",
                    "#7570B3", "#E6AB02")
pie_pal <- function(cols) {
  k <- length(cols) - 1   # named genotypes; last entry is always "Other"
  setNames(c(geno_cols_base[seq_len(k)], "grey70"), cols)
}

pie_map <- function(method, title, file_suffix) {
  pd  <- pie_data(method)
  # top-justify the pie (its top edge sits at the centroid) so every region shows the SAME
  # gap between its label and the top of its pie, regardless of pie size.
  pie_gap <- 0.035 * pie_h_span
  pc  <- pd$df %>% mutate(y = y - r)                       # pie centre = centroid - radius
  lab <- pd$df %>% transmute(region, x, y = y + pie_gap)   # label a fixed gap above the pie top
  brkN <- c(100, 1000, 10000)
  brkN <- brkN[brkN <= pd$max_n]
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = graticule,   color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = basemap,     fill = "grey95", color = "grey80", linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_sf(data = region_poly, fill = "grey88", color = "white",  linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_scatterpie(aes(x = x, y = y, group = region, r = r), data = pc,
                    cols = pd$cols, color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
    geom_text(data = lab, aes(x, y, label = region), size = 2.7, fontface = "bold") +
    # pie-area size key, placed on the right (empty South Pacific) so it groups with the
    # fill legend; smaller text than the genotype legend.
    geom_scatterpie_legend(pc$r, x = bb_pie["xmin"] + 0.82 * pie_w_span,
                           y = bb_pie["ymin"] + 0.30 * pie_h_span,
                           breaks = r_max * sqrt(brkN / pd$max_n),
                           labeller = function(r) round((r / r_max)^2 * pd$max_n), size = 2.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pie_pal(pd$cols), name = title) +
    coord_sf(datum = NA, expand = FALSE) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(text             = element_text(size = 13),
          legend.position  = "right",
          legend.key.size  = unit(0.4, "cm"),
          legend.text      = element_text(size = 7),
          legend.title     = element_text(size = 8))
  ggsave(paste0(f.out, "map_pies_", file_suffix, ".pdf"), p, width = 8.2, height = map_h)
  ggsave(paste0(f.out, "map_pies_", file_suffix, ".png"), p, width = 8.2, height = map_h)
  p
}

p_pie_genoflu <- pie_map("genoflu", "GenoFlu genotype\n(2020-2025)", "genoflu")
p_pie_genin   <- pie_map("genin",   "Genin2 genotype\n(2020-2025)",  "genin")
p_pie_genoflu
p_pie_genin
```

### Region reference map

```{r region-colours}
# colour each region by a continent-family hue ramp (base-R hcl.colors, no extra deps)
region_fam <- c(
  "Western Europe" = "Europe", "Northern Europe" = "Europe",
  "Southern Europe" = "Europe", "Eastern Europe" = "Europe",
  "Western Africa" = "Africa", "Northern Africa" = "Africa", "Southern Africa" = "Africa",
  "Eastern Africa" = "Africa", "Middle Africa" = "Africa",
  "Western Asia" = "Asia", "Central Asia" = "Asia", "Southern Asia" = "Asia",
  "South-Eastern Asia" = "Asia", "Eastern Asia" = "Asia",
  "North America" = "Americas", "Central America" = "Americas",
  "Caribbean" = "Americas", "South America" = "Americas",
  "Oceania" = "Other", "Antarctica" = "Other"
)
fam_pal <- c(Europe = "Blues 3", Africa = "Oranges", Asia = "Greens 3",
             Americas = "Purples 3", Other = "Teal")

region_cols <- unlist(lapply(names(fam_pal), function(f) {
  regs <- names(region_fam)[region_fam == f]
  # use a saturated mid-band of the ramp; the raw light end is near-white (~#F9F9F9) and reads as grey
  ramp <- colorRampPalette(hcl.colors(9, fam_pal[f])[2:7])
  setNames(ramp(length(regs)), regs)
}))
```

```{r map-region, fig.width=6, fig.height=3.5}
p_map_region <- base_map("region") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = region_cols, na.value = "grey90", guide = "none")
p_map_region
ggsave(paste0(f.out, "map_region_reference.pdf"), p_map_region, width = map_w, height = map_h)
ggsave(paste0(f.out, "map_region_reference.png"), p_map_region, width = map_w, height = map_h)
```
